glossary.definition: the parameter of an authorize request in which the app names the FHIR base it means to read from; a hospital refuses one that is not its own.
the one-time code that arrives at the redirect URI from a sign-in, which the app trades for the token.

the list of the hospitals that use a vendor's system, as the vendor publishes it in SMART's User-access Brands format: a FHIR Bundle of Organizations, each pointing to the endpoint its records are served from.
FHIR's resource that holds a list of other resources, each in an `entry`; its `type` says what the list is, such as `collection`, `history` or `searchset`.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
the name an app gives for itself when it asks to sign a patient in; a demo hospital accepts any.
the date a record gives for the thing it records, such as a result's `effectiveDateTime` or a condition's `onsetDateTime`.
a published list of codes for one kind of thing, such as RxNorm for medicines, LOINC for lab tests and SNOMED CT for clinical findings.
an entry of a record's history that says the hospital removed the record at that time; it carries no resource.
a pretend hospital with made-up patients, which an app or a test signs in to and pulls from with no account and no network; Cascade North and Cascade South are the two this package carries.
a place where one hospital's record of a person disagrees with who the person is, such as a misspelt name, which the person's `person.json` declares so that the load accepts it.
the request for a hospital's SMART configuration, with which every sign-in begins.
FHIR's resource for an address a system is reached at; in a brands bundle, a hospital's FHIR base.
the version stamp of a history entry, written `W/"<version id>"`.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: HL7's standard for health records as JSON.
the URL of a hospital's FHIR server; each record there is at `<FHIR base>/<type>/<id>`.
the HTTP header in which a go-between says which host and protocol the client asked for; `demoRemapFetch()` sends it to the listener.
the people this package made with Synthea: ten years of visits, conditions, medications and results each.
the people written by hand for tests, which this package copies from cascade-vocabulary and does not edit.
every version of one record, newest first, as a hospital answers `<type>/<id>/_history`; also the type of a patient file that holds one entry for each version.
the HTTP header in which a client says which server name it asked for.
a date and time to the second with its time zone, such as `2024-02-01T00:00:00Z`.
a story and the exports it uses, which the vocabulary carries for testing, such as `alex-rivera`.
the SMART Health IT launcher, `launch.smarthealthit.org`: a public test hospital on the internet, kept by the SMART project, which this project did not write. Its code is smart-launcher-v2.
the demo hospitals served on a port of this machine by `serveDemo()` or `npm run serve`, each at `<origin>/<id>/fhir`.
`<FHIR base>/metadata`, where a FHIR server says what it supports: the types it serves, how each is searched, and where its sign-in is.
the name of a Patient marked `use: "official"`, or its only name.
FHIR's resource for a server's warning or error message; it is no record of the patient.
FHIR's resource for a hospital, a clinic, a laboratory or another body that gives care.
the scheme, server name and port of a URL, such as `https://hospital.example`: what a browser treats as one site.
a person as one hospital knows them, under that hospital's own patient id.
the file of what one hospital holds of one person, `people/<person>/sources/<hospital>/fhir.json`: a FHIR Bundle of type `collection` or `history`.
a made-up human being, with a name, a birth date and a gender in `person.json`, who is a patient at one hospital or more.
Proof Key for Code Exchange, RFC 7636: the part of a sign-in by which an app shows, at the token exchange, that it is the app that began the sign-in. A demo hospital takes only its S256 method.
a record written once in a `collection` file, with no version: it is there at every date and is served as written.
the OPTIONS request a browser sends before a page on one origin calls a server on another, to ask whether it may.
the records one patient has at one hospital, fetched in one go: a search of each type, page by page, and a read of the Patient.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
when a hospital recorded a version, the entry's `response.lastModified`.
the app's own URL to which a hospital sends the person's browser when the sign-in is over.
public code lists, such as RxNorm for medicines, that tell an app when two codes mean one thing; the hand-written people carry codes chosen to reach them.
one record in FHIR, named by its type and its id, such as `Observation/ldl-1`.
a folder of hospital folders or of person folders that a load reads; a load takes a list of them.
what an app asks to be let read, in SMART's notation: `patient/Observation.rs` is to read and search the patient's Observations.
the type of Bundle a hospital answers a search with: one page of matches and, where there are more, a link to the next.
a way to write a record's change in a patient file as two dates, `active` and `stopped`, in place of two versions.
the page a hospital shows at its authorize address, where the patient is picked and allows or cancels what the app asks.
what a hospital's server publishes at `<FHIR base>/.well-known/smart-configuration`: where its sign-in page and its token exchange are, and what they support.
the standard by which an app signs a person in to a hospital and is then let read that person's records: OAuth 2.0 as HL7's SMART App Launch profiles it for FHIR servers.
what one hospital holds of one person: the folder `sources/<hospital>/` of the person, with a patient file, C-CDA documents, or both.
a value the app sends with the authorize request and the hospital sends back unchanged, so the app can tell its own sign-in's answer.
a made-up patient at a demo hospital whose records were written to show one outcome, such as a lab result that falls after a medication starts, with that outcome written down beside them.
an open-source program that makes up whole patient histories; the generated people came from it.
the access token a hospital issues when a person signs in: the credential an app sends with each request for that person's records.
the secret a hospital signs its tokens with (`hospital.json`'s `key`).
OAuth's error for a client the server does not accept; the token exchange answers 401 with it. The launcher's switch for it is named `token_invalid_token`, which differs from the error it gives.
the request in which an app trades the authorization code for the token.
what a record says at one time; when a hospital changes a record, its history keeps the old version and adds a new one.
the date a hospital answers for, an instant given as `asOf`: it serves each record as it stood then. With none, it serves each record's latest version.
